newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon says not affected by ex-chief move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon says not affected by ex-chief move.

text.p: Taiwan's leading microchip maker Taiwan Semiconductor said on Thursday its business would not be affected by its former president Donald Brooks' decision to join rival chipmaker United Microelectronics.
"Taiwan Semiconductor's solid customer relationship will not be easily affected by Mr Brooks' joining United Microelectronics," company spokesman Y.C. Huang said in a statement.
On Wednesday, United Microelectronics said it had given a senior post to Donald Brooks, who until April was president of Taiwan Semiconductor.
Brooks was named a director on United Micro's board and given the post of president of international operations.
Taiwan Semiconductor is the first and the largest integrated circuits foundry in the world, and has a long-standing relationship with its customers, spokesman Huang said.
"The company is very confident with its future development and is working on new investment as planned," Huang said.

Within days of Brooks' departure, Taiwan Semiconductor announced a T$400 billion, 10-year plan to build several advanced wafer fabrication plants in a new high-tech park in southern Tainan -- the biggest investment in Taiwan to date.
Less than three months later United Micro unveiled its own huge development scheme, bigger by T$100 billion and to be based in the same Tainan science park.
Taiwan Semiconductor has announced it would recruit Dr. Chiang Shang-yi to be its vice-president in charge of research and development, the statement said.
Chiang joins Taiwan Semiconductor from Hewlett-Packard, where he worked for 17 years and was heavily involoved in research and development, it said.
